recipes.name: Carlee's Celebrate Spring Cupcakes
ingredients_raw: 2 (3.9 ounce) packages instant chocolate pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease two 12-cup cupcake tins or line with paper liners.
Combine cake mix, water, eggs, and oil in a large bowl; beat with an electric mixer on medium speed until well combined, about 2 minutes. Spoon batter into the prepared cups, filling each ⅔ full.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into centers comes out clean, 19 to 23 minutes. Cool cupcakes completely.
Beat milk and pudding mix together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until thick, about 2 minutes; beat in whipped topping.

Fit a pastry bag with a coupler and a large piping tip. Drop piping bag into a tall glass and fold edges down around the glass. Spoon about 1 ½ cups pudding mixture into the bag; gather edges and twist together. Set aside remaining pudding mixture.
Press piping tip into center of each cupcake; fill each with about 1 ½ tablespoons pudding mixture.
Spoon 1 heaping tablespoon remaining pudding mixture on top of each cupcake; swirl to make a nest. Press chocolate sprinkles around edges of nests; place 3 chocolate eggs in each nest.

raw_recipe.headline: Carlee's Celebrate Spring Cupcakes
raw_recipe.description: Carlee's celebrate spring cupcakes recipe features creamy chocolate centers and a cute little bird's nest on top filled with mini chocolate eggs.

review.reviewBody: What a wonderful cupcake! I made these this afternoon with my little guy and we had a blast. The creamy filling/frosting is absolutely delicious and I definitely will be using it for other cupcakes as well. Thanks for sharing this cute, easy and fun cupcake!

Recipe was very easy to make. However I followed exactly as instructed - filling and topping 1)was not as thick & chocolate as appears in pic. 2) it made way too much for 24cupcakes 3)perhaps use the 2 pkg of pudding, 1 cup of milk and 8 oz of whipped topping.
These were really cute! And they tasted great too. Good job!
I used the birds nest idea for fun. I didn't turn out how I had planned, but overall a great idea!
I used jelly beans, and the bird's nests didn't really work out for me, but they tasted great. I just whipped cream, and it was a wonderful idea to combine that and pudding for a unique frosting!
These are fantastic with peanut butter M&Ms!
These were so adorable! I loved them.

idea and appearance for sure gets a 5 - - taste is a 3, so i will round out a 4. boxed cake mix and pudding do not make a great cupcake imho.... i made it for the kids for our easter dessert table and they all seemed to enjoy them. however i have several leftover that i fear will get tossed, as the taste is just not worth the calories! if i were to make this recipe again, it would be with a homemade cake and frosting recipe, and just borrowing the idea for the birds nest. all in all though, they make a great presentation and are very easy to make. thanks for posting this great idea!

These were definately a hit with my family and kiddos. Made a Duncan Hines devils food cake and for the frosting, I used sugar free/fat free chocolate pudding, skim milk and fat free whipped topping. Delicious and light! Kiddos decorated them with the chocolate sprinkles and Cadbury mini candy coated eggs. Thanks!
